cards.anchor: Hypothesized preservation of the bounded outcome: three elevation-vial attenuations with normalized spread at most 4 percent at second 120, using 30 stirring seconds instead of a matched 60-second rotation comparator. The stipulated successful 300 rpm trial supports that comparator only once; savings against the preferred 900 rpm procedure remain unknown.
cards.burden: Six fresh trials in two three-condition blocks consume the entire session allowance. The hybrid exchanges 30 stirring seconds for three manual syringe cycles; record transfer count, timing and execution failures, without claiming reduced total effort or energy. Use the spill tray, stop if liquid escapes, and report every target failure. All mixing ends at second 60, within the second-105 ceiling.
cards.construction: Hypothesis: low-to-high syringe turnover can substitute for part of rotation. With the stipulated recipe, command 300 rpm during seconds 0-15, stop rotation, withdraw 20 mL at the marked low position and return it at the marked upper-side position three times during seconds 15-45, then command 300 rpm during seconds 45-60. Stop all mixing at second 60 and sample at second 120. The terminal rotation is intended to distribute each returned plume; neither this mechanism nor success has been observed.
cards.defeat: The tested construction fails the outcome if its final spread exceeds 4 percent. Repeated hybrid failure alongside successful continuous-rotation comparators defeats reliable substitution in this session. Hybrid readings resembling the short-rotation arm while only continuous rotation passes defeat the predicted transfer rescue. If both short arms pass, transfer necessity is unsupported and the added work earns no demonstrated benefit. If all arms fail, the comparator does not establish an opening. Inability to complete transfers by second 45 is an execution failure; do not extend or repair the trial.
cards.mutation: Compose the available rotation and syringe parent operations into a timer-controlled construction, replacing part of the rotational duty with low-to-high turnover and severing optical spread from commands. Match the last stirring interval and final quiet period across all three arms so unequal cessation times do not explain their final-vial differences.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis prediction: in both blocks the hybrid and continuous 60-second arms meet the at-most-4-percent sample criterion, while the matched 30-second arm without transfers exceeds it. This pattern supports a transfer contribution to this composite construction and an observed 30-second stirring reduction against its local comparator, with only two repeats per arm.
cards.prediction_rival: Rival prediction: if transfers mostly circulate local parcels and leave the relevant depth gradients, the hybrid resembles the short-rotation arm and both exceed 4 percent, while the continuous arm meets the criterion. Alternatively, all arms passing would support sufficient short rotation or a common measurement effect rather than the claimed transfer rescue.
cards.probe: Use two blocks of three fresh recipes. Block one runs continuous 300 rpm during seconds 0-60, short rotation during 0-15 and 45-60 with an undisturbed middle pause, then the hybrid. Reverse that condition order in block two. Use one dye bottle, fixed addition location, rinsed vessel and locked camera; obtain water-only and common-aliquot references per block. All arms stop rotation at 60, remain quiet until 120, and yield 1 mL at each marked depth within ten seconds. Alternate low-to-high and high-to-low sampling order across successive trials, giving each condition both orders. Log side frames and spread every five seconds without letting them control operation; record nominal commands, all transfer times, vial readings, reference repeatability and failures. Compare the hybrid with the identical short schedule to test transfer contribution, and with continuous rotation to test preserved outcome with fewer stirring seconds. No additional pause pair fits these six trials.
cards.rival: Hypothesis: sustained bulk rotation supplies transport that a few syringe returns cannot replace; local return plumes or rewithdrawal of recently returned liquid leave unsampled gradients. Sampling disturbance or a shared optical bias could also make all final vials agree without establishing pre-sampling concentration uniformity.
unknowns: Only two repeats per condition are possible; reversed condition order and alternating sampling order reduce selected confounds but do not eliminate drift or prove reliability.
The nominal speeds lack independent tachometer verification, and common-aliquot repeatability is not concentration calibration. Final vials remain a bounded optical proxy.

Withdrawals, returns and final sampling can disturb gradients. Any supported effect belongs to this specified transfer-plus-rotation construction; it does not establish uniformity at every location or earlier time.

Specks do not identify bubbles. This probe neither measures bubble fraction nor establishes the proposed agitation-to-optical feedback loop; those unavailable measurements are not required for its sample-proxy comparison.
The selected six-trial probe uses no additional matched pause pair. The received seconds-45-to-50 pause option remains pending rather than an observed result.
Manual transfers may increase work despite reducing stirring seconds. Preferred-procedure duration and applicability to other liquids, vessels or continuous processes remain unknown.
